allocation_status: Teaching design; verified source has no official lesson count.
rationale: Twelve40minute lessons separate lever-arm geometry/units/sense,force+moment balance,actual approved ruler demonstration and uncertainty,anti-parallel pure/unequal pairs,applications/actual observation,synthesis and independent final. Actual demonstration/route/digital provision must be recorded or remain unperformed.
prerequisites: Forces in newtons,metre/centimetre conversion,multiplication and signed sums.
Read plane axes and distinguish an ideal model from measurements.
teacher_confirmation_required: Approve stable low support,light rule,secured loads no more than1N each,clear drop/pinch zones and supervised setup/removal before actual TF5.
Find actual unloaded rule balance point;do not assume50cm or ignore off-centre weight.
Record actual measured loads/distances/roles/balance and uncertainty;supplied TF6 does not certify demonstration.
Approve designated safe school route/privacy/no-operation limits;otherwise use supplied cards and record walk not performed.
Provide and preview digital moments/couple resources if available;print cards do not establish animation viewing or research.
Confirm sign conventions,accessibility,40minute pacing and product/tool limits.

lesson_map.title: How do units and unknown forces connect?
How do force direction and position set turning sense?
What conditions balance an ideal bar?
Can an actual metre rule demonstrate the principle?
How should a small balance mismatch be interpreted?
Why can equal opposite forces still turn a body?
When are anti-parallel forces not a couple?
How can a turning model support a practical choice?
Where are moments used around the school?
Which moment claims withstand an audit?
Can turning-effect evidence support an independent explanation?
